scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The nightly audit job against super_spine_router_0 started failing:
route-table queries on that device return daemon-connection errors,
and interface state can no longer be read through the FRR CLI. Oddly,
both spine routers still show their BGP session to the super-spine as
Established, and no user traffic is affected -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and
pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reach each other normally. Figure out what is wrong
on super_spine_router_0.

injection.action: kill the zebra daemon (and watchfrr) on super_spine_router_0

post_inject_check.expect: 0% loss   (still OK -- the super-spine is not on the pc_0_0<->pc_0_1 path)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: super_spine_router_0 zebra
Mechanism: zebra is FRR's RIB/kernel-interface daemon. It was killed
  together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it, while
  bgpd keeps running: the BGP sessions to spine_router_0_0
  (172.16.0.1) and spine_router_0_1 (172.16.0.3) stay Established
  because bgpd owns its own TCP sessions. The failure is in the
  management/route-programming plane: zebra-owned CLI queries (route
  table, interface state) fail, and bgpd can no longer program new
  routes into the kernel. Forwarding continues on the kernel FIB that
  zebra had already installed (a SIGKILL leaves kernel routes in
  place), and in this size-s fabric the super-spine is not even on the
  pc_0_0 <-> pc_0_1 data path (that path is leaf -> spine -> leaf), so
  there is no user impact -- but the device would blackhole any future
  route change it needs zebra to program.
Localization: super_spine_router_0
Root cause: zebra not running on super_spine_router_0 (bgpd still up)
Fix: restart FRR on super_spine_router_0 (`service frr restart`) --
  the config persists in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart brings back
  zebra, watchfrr and bgpd cleanly.

Observable note: the kill uses the same watchfrr-first pattern as the
lab-verified bgpd kills on this fabric (nothing respawns the daemon).
With zebra dead but bgpd alive, `pgrep zebra` is empty while
`pgrep bgpd` still returns a process; zebra-owned vtysh queries (e.g.
the route table) error out while BGP state remains queryable from the
peers. An agent that describes this as "FRR is partially down /
zebra crashed on super_spine_router_0" has found the fault.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on super_spine_router_0. The persistent
/etc/frr/frr.conf restores zebra (and watchfrr) alongside bgpd; the
route-programming and CLI/telemetry plane recovers, and the BGP
sessions re-establish.

must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: BGP sessions remain Established and traffic flows while zebra-owned queries/route programming fail
bonus-explains-stale-fib: explains that forwarding continues on the already-installed kernel FIB (and/or that the super-spine is not on the pc_0_0<->pc_0_1 data path)

line.expect: 0% loss   (still OK -- the super-spine is not on the pc_0_0<->pc_0_1 path)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: FRR’s Zebra daemon and service supervision on super_spine_router_0. The mgmtd/bgpd/staticd processes are up, but zebra (the RIB/interface manager) is down and frr.service is not supervising the stack.

Mechanism: The nightly audit queries the route table and interfaces via the FRR CLI (vtysh/mgmtd). Those requests depend on zebra’s southbound sockets. With zebra absent, FRR returns daemon-connection errors and “zebra is not running” for route/interface commands, even though BGP sessions themselves can remain established.

Localization and evidence: On super_spine_router_0:
- frr show ip route reports: “zebra is not running.”
- systemctl status frr: Active: inactive (dead).
- Process list shows only mgmtd, bgpd, staticd; no zebra.
- /var/log/frr/frr.log contains zebra startup lines at 19:29:42–43, after which zebra disappears, indicating it started and then exited.
Meanwhile the spines show BGP Established with the super-spine, and super_spine_router_0’s own “show bgp summary” is healthy, explaining why user traffic between 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 is unaffected.

Root cause: The zebra daemon on super_spine_router_0 terminated (or was never kept under supervision), while bgpd/mgmtd continued running; the FRR service unit is inactive, so zebra is not restarted.

Corrective fix: Restore proper FRR supervision and bring zebra up. Recommended: enable and restart the FRR service so watchfrr manages all daemons (systemctl enable --now frr; or systemctl restart frr). Verify /etc/frr/daemons has zebra=yes (it does) and remove any ad‑hoc starts of individual daemons. After restart, confirm vtysh “show ip route” and “show interface” succeed.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names and provides evidence from super_spine_router_0 (e.g., process list, systemctl status, log lines), satisfying the device identification requirement.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes that bgpd remains up and BGP sessions are Established and traffic unaffected while zebra is down causing zebra-owned CLI/route-programming errors, matching the required symptom pattern.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes traffic is unaffected but fails to explain that forwarding continues on the previously installed kernel FIB (or that the super-spine is not on the pc_0_0<->pc_0_1 data path); it incorrectly attributes lack of impact to BGP being 'healthy' rather than stale kernel routes remaining.
Recommends enabling/restarting the FRR service so watchfrr supervises and restarts zebra (and verifying daemons config), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log contains the precise observations (zebra CLI error, frr.service inactive, ps output lacking zebra, daemons file showing zebra=yes, FRR logs, BGP summaries on peers, and host reachability) that back the agent's diagnosis; the inference that zebra is down while bgpd remains and that restarting the FRR service will restore zebra is logical and well-supported.
